sentences.zh: =姚南仲=姚南仲，華州下邽人。

translations.literal: Yao Nanzhong was a native of Xiaji in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Nanzhong came from Xiaji in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，制科登第，授太子校書，歷高陵、昭應、萬年三縣尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era, he passed the special examination and was appointed Crown Prince's collator; he served successively as county magistrate of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianyuan period he passed the special examination, was made collator to the Crown Prince, and served in turn as magistrate of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian counties.

sentences.zh: 遷右拾遺，轉右補闕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Reminder and then transferred to Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Reminder and then became Right Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 大歷十三年，貞懿皇后獨孤氏崩，代宗悼惜不已，令於近城為陵墓，冀朝夕臨望於目前。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of the Dali era, the Virtuous and Gracious Empress of the Dugu clan died; Emperor Daizong mourned her without cease and ordered a tomb built near the city, hoping to gaze upon it morning and evening before his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 13 the Virtuous and Gracious Empress, née Dugu, died. Emperor Daizong grieved deeply and ordered a mausoleum built close to the capital so he could look upon it at every hour of the day.

sentences.zh: 南仲上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Nanzhong submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong submitted a memorial of remonstrance, which read:

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝甚嘉之，賜緋魚袋，特加五品階，宣付史館。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor greatly praised it, bestowed a crimson fish pouch, specially added five ranks, and ordered it proclaimed to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor greatly praised it, granted him a crimson fish pouch, specially raised him five ranks, and ordered the text deposited in the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 與宰相常袞善，袞貶官，南仲坐出為海鹽縣令。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with the chief minister Chang Gun; when Gun was demoted, Nanzhong was implicated and sent out as magistrate of Haiyan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was friendly with Chief Minister Chang Gun. When Gun was demoted, Nanzhong was implicated and sent out as magistrate of Haiyan County.

sentences.zh: 浙江東、西道觀察使韓滉辟為推官，奏授殿中侍御史、內供奉，充支使。

translations.literal: Han Huang, observation commissioner of the eastern and western circuits of Zhejiang, recruited him as investigating officer; he memorialized to appoint him Palace Diarist, inner attendant, and supply commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, commissioner observing the eastern and western Zhejiang circuits, recruited him as investigating officer and memorialized to make him Palace Diarist and inner attendant, with duty as supply commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋征還，歷左司兵部員外，轉郎中，遷御史中丞、給事中、同州刺史、陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled, served as Left Secretariat and Ministry of War vice director, was transferred to director, and was promoted to Censor-in-Chief, Drafting Attendant, prefect of Tongzhou, and observation commissioner of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled, served as vice director in the Left Secretariat and Ministry of War, became director, and rose to Censor-in-Chief, Drafting Attendant, prefect of Tongzhou, and commissioner observing Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年，代李復為鄭滑節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he replaced Li Fu as military commissioner of Zheng-Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 15 he replaced Li Fu as military commissioner of Zheng-Hua.

sentences.zh: 監軍薛盈珍恃勢奪軍政，南仲數為盈珍讒毀，德宗頗疑之。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Xue Yingzhen relied on his power to seize military administration; Nanzhong was repeatedly slandered by Yingzhen, and Dezong came to doubt him considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisor Xue Yingzhen used his power to seize control of military affairs. Yingzhen slandered Nanzhong repeatedly, and Dezong grew quite suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，盈珍遣小使程務盈馳驛奉表，誣奏南仲陰事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Yingzhen sent the minor envoy Cheng Wuying by express relay with a memorial falsely accusing Nanzhong of secret matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Yingzhen sent his aide Cheng Wuying by express relay with a memorial falsely accusing Nanzhong of secret wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 南仲裨將曹文洽亦入奏事京師，伺知盈珍表中語。

translations.literal: Nanzhong's lieutenant Cao Wenqia also entered the capital to report on affairs and learned the wording of Yingzhen's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong's lieutenant Cao Wenqia had also come to the capital on official business and learned what Yingzhen's memorial said.

sentences.zh: 文洽私懷憤怒，遂晨夜兼道追務盈，至長樂驛及之，與同舍宿；

translations.literal: Wenqia privately harbored anger, then day and night by double stages pursued Wuying, overtook him at Changle Post, and lodged in the same quarters;
translations.idiomatic: Wenqia burned with private rage and pursued Wuying day and night by forced marches. He overtook him at Changle Post and lodged in the same inn;

sentences.zh: 中夜殺務盈，沈盈珍表於廁中，乃自殺。

translations.literal: at midnight he killed Wuying, sank Yingzhen's memorial in the privy, and then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: at midnight he killed Wuying, sank Yingzhen's memorial in the privy, and then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 日旰，驛吏辟門，見血流塗地，旁得文洽二緘，一告於南仲，一表理南仲之冤，且陳首殺務盈。

translations.literal: At sundown the post attendant opened the door, saw blood spread across the ground, and beside it found two letters from Wenqia—one reporting to Nanzhong, one stating Nanzhong's innocence and confessing that he had killed Wuying first.
translations.idiomatic: At sundown the post attendant opened the door and found blood spread across the ground. Beside the bodies lay two letters from Wenqia: one to Nanzhong and one pleading Nanzhong's innocence and confessing that he had killed Wuying.

sentences.zh: 上聞其事，頗駭異之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of the affair, he was greatly startled and astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of the affair, he was deeply startled.

sentences.zh: 南仲慮釁深，遂乞入朝。

translations.literal: Nanzhong, fearing the breach was deep, then begged to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the breach was grave, Nanzhong asked to come to court.

sentences.zh: 德宗曰：「盈珍擾軍政耶？」

translations.literal: Dezong said: 'Did Yingzhen interfere with military administration?
translations.idiomatic: Dezong asked, 'Did Yingzhen interfere with military administration?

sentences.zh: 南仲對曰：「勇珍不擾軍政，臣自隳陛下法耳。

translations.literal: Nanzhong replied: 'Yingzhen did not interfere with military administration; it is I who have myself destroyed Your Majesty's law.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong replied, 'Yingzhen did not interfere with military affairs. I am the one who has broken Your Majesty's law.

sentences.zh: 如盈珍輩所在有之，雖羊、杜復生，撫百姓，禦三軍，必不能成愷悌父母之政，師律善陣之制矣。」

translations.literal: Where men like Yingzhen exist everywhere, even if Yang Xiong and Du Fu were reborn, in comforting the people and commanding the three armies they could certainly not achieve a parental government of kindness and ease or the discipline of army law and good formations.'
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yingzhen are everywhere. Even if Yang Xiong and Du Fu were reborn, they could not comfort the people and command the armies while achieving a parental rule of kindness or the discipline of proper formations and army law.'

sentences.zh: 上默然久之。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent for a long time.

sentences.zh: 授尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 貞元十九年七月，終於位，年七十四，贈太子太保，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan he died in office at age seventy-four; he was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with posthumous title Upright.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhenyuan 19 he died in office at seventy-four. He was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Upright.

sentences.zh: =劉迺=劉迺，字永夷，洺州廣平人。

translations.literal: Liu Nai, courtesy name Yongyi, was a native of Guangping in Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Nai, courtesy name Yongyi, came from Guangping in Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖武幹，武德初拜侍中，即中書侍郎林甫從祖兄子也。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Wu Gan was appointed Palace Attendant at the beginning of Wude; he was the son of the paternal cousin of Zhongshu Vice Director Linpu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wu Gan was made Palace Attendant at the start of the Wude era; he was a cousin of Zhongshu Vice Director Linpu.

sentences.zh: 父如璠，昫山丞，以迺貴，贈民部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Ru Fan was assistant magistrate of Xushan; because of Nai's eminence he was posthumously made Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ru Fan had been assistant magistrate of Xushan; because of Nai's eminence he was posthumously made director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 迺少聰穎誌學，暗記《六經》，日數千言。

translations.literal: Nai in youth was clever and eager to learn, memorized the Six Classics by heart, and recited several thousand words a day.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Nai was clever and eager to learn. He memorized the Six Classics and could recite several thousand words a day.

sentences.zh: 及長，文章清雅，為當時推重。

translations.literal: When grown, his writing was refined and elegant and was esteemed in his time.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age his writing was refined and elegant, and his contemporaries held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，舉進士，尋丁父艱，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination; soon after he entered mourning for his father and was known for filial conduct in bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination. He soon mourned his father and became known for filial conduct during bereavement.

sentences.zh: 既終制，從調選曹。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he followed the selection bureau for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he went to the selection bureau for assignment.

sentences.zh: 迺常以文部選才未為盡善，遂致書於知銓舍人宋昱曰：

translations.literal: Nai often considered that the Ministry of Rites' selection of talent was not fully adequate and therefore sent a letter to Selection Attendant Song Yu, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Nai often felt that the Ministry of Rites did not select talent as well as it might, and wrote to Selection Attendant Song Yu, saying:

sentences.zh: 《虞書》稱：「知人則哲，能官人則惠。」

translations.literal: The Documents of Yu says: 'To know men is to be wise; to be able to assign men to offices is to be gracious.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents of Yu says, 'To know men is wisdom; to place men in office is grace.'

sentences.zh: 巍巍唐、虞，舉以為難。

translations.literal: The august eras of Tang and Yu regarded it as difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Even the august eras of Tang and Yu found this difficult.

sentences.zh: 今夫文部，既始之以掄材，終之以授位，是則知人官人，斯為重任。

translations.literal: Now the Ministry of Rites begins with weighing talent and ends with conferring office—thus to know men and assign them to office is a weighty charge.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Ministry of Rites begins by weighing talent and ends by conferring office. Knowing men and placing them in office is therefore a weighty charge.

sentences.zh: 昔在禹、稷、臯陶之眾聖，猶曰載采有九德，考績以九載。

translations.literal: Of old, among the many sages Yu, Ji, and Gao Yao, it was still said that one must gather and test the nine virtues and examine achievement over nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Of old, even among sages such as Yu, Ji, and Gao Yao, it was said that one must gather and test the nine virtues and examine achievement over nine years.

sentences.zh: 近代主司，獨委一二小冢宰，察言於一幅之判，觀行於一揖之內，古今遲速，何不侔之甚哉！

translations.literal: In recent times the chief examiners entrust it solely to one or two minor selection officials, examining words in a single sheet of judgment and observing conduct within one bow—how greatly ancient and modern differ in speed!
translations.idiomatic: Today the chief examiners leave the task to one or two minor selection officers, judging words from a single examination essay and conduct from a single bow. How vast is the gap between antiquity and the present!

sentences.zh: 夫判者，以狹詞短韻，語有定規為體，亦猶以一小冶而鼓眾金，雖欲為鼎為鏞，不可得也。

translations.literal: Judgment essays take narrow words and short rhymes with fixed rules as their form—it is like using a small furnace to smelt all metals: though one wishes to make cauldrons and bells, it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment essay uses narrow diction, short rhymes, and fixed rules. It is like smelting all metals in a small furnace: one may wish to cast cauldrons and bells, but cannot.

sentences.zh: 故曰：判之在文，至局促者。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said that judgment in literary form is the most cramped.
translations.idiomatic: That is why they say the judgment essay is the most cramped form of writing.

sentences.zh: 夫銓者，必以崇衣冠，自媒耀為賢，斯又士之醜行，君子所病。

translations.literal: In selection one must esteem dress and cap and self-display as talent—this again is the ugly conduct of scholars, what gentlemen deplore.
translations.idiomatic: Selection favors fine dress and self-display as marks of talent—ugly habits among scholars, and what gentlemen deplore.

sentences.zh: 若引文公、尼父登之於銓廷，則雖圖書《易象》之大訓，以判體挫之，曾不及徐、庾。

translations.literal: If Duke Wen of Jin and the Master were brought to the selection hall, though they had the great teachings of the classics and the Changes, judged by the essay form they would not even match Xu or Yu.
translations.idiomatic: If Duke Wen of Jin and Confucius stood in the selection hall, their great teachings in the classics and Changes would be judged by the essay form and would rank below Xu and Yu.

sentences.zh: 雖有至德，以喋喋取之，曾不若嗇夫。

translations.literal: Though possessing utmost virtue, if taken by glib talk they would not even equal a miser.
translations.idiomatic: Though possessed of utmost virtue, if judged by glib talk they would rank below a miser.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 彼幹霄蔽日，誠巨樹也，當求尺寸之材，必後於椓杙。

translations.literal: Those trees that pierce the clouds and shade the sun are truly great trees, yet when seeking timber by the foot they must come after stakes and pegs.
translations.idiomatic: Trees that pierce the clouds and shade the sun are truly great timber, yet when boards are measured by the foot they rank behind stakes and pegs.

sentences.zh: 龍吟武嘯，誠希聲也，若尚頰舌之感，必下於蛙黽。

translations.literal: The dragon's chant and tiger's roar are truly rare sounds; if cheek and tongue impressions are valued, they must rank below frogs and toads.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon's chant and tiger's roar are rare sounds indeed; if glib speech is prized, they must rank below frogs and toads.

sentences.zh: 觀察之際，猶不悲夫！

translations.literal: At the time of observation—is this not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: When one considers this—is it not lamentable!

sentences.zh: 執事慮過龜策，文合雅誥，豈拘以瑣瑣故事，曲折因循哉？

translations.literal: Your office's deliberations surpass tortoise and yarrow, your writing accords with elegant decrees—how can one be bound by petty precedents and twist and turn in compliance?
translations.idiomatic: Your deliberations surpass divination by tortoise and yarrow, and your writing matches the elegant decrees. Surely you need not be bound by petty precedent and twist every way in compliance?

sentences.zh: 誠能先資以政事，次征以文學，退觀其理家，進察其臨節，則厖鴻深沈之事，亦可以窺其門戶矣！

translations.literal: If one truly first relies on administrative affairs, next examines literary learning, withdraws to observe how they manage the household, and advances to inspect how they face critical moments, then even vast and profound matters may be glimpsed through their doorway!
translations.idiomatic: If you first weigh administrative ability, then literary accomplishment, observe how candidates manage their households in private life, and test how they face crisis, even vast and profound matters may be glimpsed through the doorway of their character!

sentences.zh: 其載，補剡縣尉，改會稽尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed supplemental magistrate of Shan County and transferred to magistrate of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed supplemental magistrate of Shan County and transferred to magistrate of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 宣州觀察使殷日用奏為判官，宣慰使李季卿又以表薦，連授大理評事、兼監察御史。

translations.literal: Yin Riyong, observation commissioner of Xuanzhou, memorialized to appoint him judge; the pacification commissioner Li Jiqing also recommended him by memorial, and he was successively made Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Riyong, commissioner observing Xuanzhou, memorialized to make him judge; pacification commissioner Li Jiqing also recommended him, and he was successively made evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 轉運使劉晏奏令巡覆江西，多所蠲免。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan memorialized to have him tour and review Jiangxi, and many remissions were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan had him tour and review Jiangxi, and many tax remissions were granted.

sentences.zh: 改殿中侍御史、檢校倉部員外、民部郎中，並充浙西留後。

translations.literal: He was changed to Palace Diarist, acting vice director of the Granaries Office, and director in the Ministry of Revenue, all while serving as acting governor of western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Diarist, acting vice director of the Granaries Office, and director in the Ministry of Revenue, while serving as acting governor of western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 佐晏征賦，頗有裨益，晏甚任之。

translations.literal: Assisting Yan in collecting taxes, he was of considerable benefit, and Yan greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting Yan in tax collection, he proved of considerable benefit, and Yan relied on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 大歷十二年，元載既誅，以迺久在職，召拜司門員外郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dali, after Yuan Zai was executed, because Nai had long served in office he was summoned and appointed vice director of the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 12, after Yuan Zai was executed, Nai was summoned to court because of his long service and appointed vice director of the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 十四年，崔祐甫秉政，素與迺友善。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Cui Youfu held power; he had long been friendly with Nai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Cui Youfu took power; he had long been friendly with Nai.

sentences.zh: 會加郭子儀尚父，以冊禮久廢，至是復行之。

translations.literal: It happened that Guo Ziyi was given the title Exalted Father; the enfeoffment rites had long been abandoned and were now revived.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was given the title Exalted Father. The enfeoffment rites had long fallen into disuse and were now revived.

sentences.zh: 祐甫令兩省官撰冊文，未稱旨；

translations.literal: Youfu ordered officials of the two departments to draft the enfeoffment text, but it did not please;
translations.idiomatic: Youfu had officials of the two departments draft the enfeoffment text, but none pleased the throne;

sentences.zh: 召迺至閣草之，立就。

translations.literal: Nai was summoned to the pavilion to draft it and finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: Nai was summoned to the pavilion to draft it and finished at once.

sentences.zh: 詞義典裁，祐甫嘆賞久之。

translations.literal: The wording and meaning were classical and measured; Youfu sighed in admiration for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The wording was classical and measured. Youfu sighed in admiration for a long time.

sentences.zh: 數日，擢為給事中，尋遷權知兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Within days he was promoted to Drafting Attendant and soon transferred to acting Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was promoted to Drafting Attendant and soon made acting Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 及楊炎、盧杞為相，意多醜正，以故五歲不遷。

translations.literal: When Yang Yan and Lu Qi became chancellors, they mostly detested the upright, and for this reason for five years he was not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan and Lu Qi became chancellors, they mostly detested upright men, and for five years he received no promotion.

sentences.zh: 建中四年夏，但真拜而已。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Jianzhong he received only a regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jianzhong 4 he received only a regular appointment to the post.

sentences.zh: 其冬，涇師作亂，駕幸奉天。

translations.literal: That winter the Jing army mutinied and the imperial carriage went to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Jing army mutinied and the emperor fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 迺臥疾在私第，賊泚遣使以甘言誘之，乃稱疾篤。

translations.literal: Nai lay ill in his private residence; the rebel Zhu Ci sent envoys with sweet words to entice him, and he claimed his illness was severe.
translations.idiomatic: Nai lay ill at home. The rebel Zhu Ci sent envoys with flattering words to entice him, and Nai claimed his illness was grave.

sentences.zh: 又令其偽宰相蔣鎮自來招誘，迺托喑疾，灸灼遍身。

translations.literal: Ci also had his false chancellor Jiang Zhen come in person to recruit him; Nai pleaded aphasia and had moxibustion burns over his whole body.
translations.idiomatic: Ci also sent his false chancellor Jiang Zhen in person to recruit him. Nai feigned aphasia and had moxibustion burns applied all over his body.

sentences.zh: 鎮再至，知不可劫脅，乃嘆息曰：「鎮亦嘗忝列曹郎，茍不能死，以至於斯，寧以自辱膻腥，復欲汙穢賢哲乎？」

translations.literal: When Zhen came again and knew he could not be coerced, he sighed and said: 'I too once served among the bureau directors; if I could not die, it has come to this—how can I further shame myself with the stench of mutton and fish and again wish to defile worthy sages?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen came again and saw coercion would not work, he sighed and said, 'I too once served among the bureau directors. Having failed to die then, I have come to this. How can I further shame myself with the rebels' stench and again try to defile a worthy man?

sentences.zh: 歔欷而退。

translations.literal: He sobbed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及聞輿駕再幸梁州，乃自投於床，搏膺呼天，因是危惙，絕食數日而卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: When he heard the imperial carriage had again gone to Liangzhou, he threw himself upon the bed, beat his breast and called to Heaven, and thereby fell into critical illness; after fasting several days he died at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the emperor had again fled to Liangzhou, he threw himself on his bed, beat his breast, and cried to Heaven. He fell critically ill, fasted for several days, and died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 德宗還京，聞迺之忠烈，追贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Dezong returned to the capital and heard of Nai's loyal martyrdom, he posthumously made him Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong returned to the capital and heard of Nai's loyal martyrdom, he posthumously made him Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子伯芻。

translations.literal: His son was Boqu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Boqu.

sentences.zh: 伯芻，字素芝，登進士第，誌行修謹。

translations.literal: Boqu, courtesy name Suzhi, passed the jinshi examination; his conduct and aims were cultivated and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Boqu, courtesy name Suzhi, passed the jinshi examination. His conduct was cultivated and careful.

sentences.zh: 淮南杜佑辟為從事，府罷，屏居吳中。

translations.literal: Du You of Huainan recruited him as staff officer; when the office was abolished, he lived in seclusion in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Du You of Huainan recruited him as staff officer. When the office closed, he lived in seclusion in the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 久之，征拜右補闕，遷主客員外郎。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned and appointed Right Supplementation Censor and promoted to vice director of the Hosts Office.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was summoned as Right Supplementation Censor and promoted to vice director of the Hosts Office.

sentences.zh: 以過從友人飲噱，為韋執誼密奏，貶虔州掾曹，復為考功員外郎裴垍善其應對機捷，遷考功郎中、集賢院學士，轉給事中。

translations.literal: For excessive drinking and jesting with friends he was secretly memorialized against by Wei Zhiyi and demoted to clerical officer of Qianzhou; later as vice director of merit evaluation, Pei Ji appreciated his quick and nimble responses and he was promoted to director of merit evaluation, academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and transferred to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He drank and jested too freely with friends; Wei Zhiyi secretly memorialized against him and he was demoted to a clerical post in Qianzhou. Later, as vice director of merit evaluation, he impressed Pei Ji with his quick wit and rose to director of merit evaluation, academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 裴垍罷相，為太子賓客，未幾而卒。

translations.literal: When Pei Ji left the chancellorship he became Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died before long.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Ji left office he became Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫復入相，與垍宿嫌，不加贈官；

translations.literal: When Li Jifu returned to the chancellorship, he bore an old grudge against Ji and did not grant posthumous office;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu returned as chancellor, he bore an old grudge against Ji and granted no posthumous office;

sentences.zh: 伯芻上疏論之，贈垍太子少傅。

translations.literal: Boqu submitted a memorial arguing the point, and Ji was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Boqu submitted a memorial on the matter, and Ji was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 伯芻妻，垍從姨也。

translations.literal: Boqu's wife was Ji's maternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Boqu's wife was Ji's maternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 或讒於吉甫，此以論奏。

translations.literal: Some slandered him to Jifu, saying this memorial was for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: Some told Jifu the memorial was motivated by family ties.

sentences.zh: 伯芻懼，亟請散地，因出為虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Boqu grew afraid, urgently requested a loose post, and was therefore sent out as prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Boqu grew afraid, urgently asked for a less prominent post, and was sent out as prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 吉甫卒，裴度擢為刑部侍郎，俄知吏部選事。

translations.literal: When Jifu died, Pei Du promoted him to Vice Minister of Justice and soon had him oversee selection affairs in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Jifu died, Pei Du promoted him to Vice Minister of Justice and soon put him in charge of personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，以左常侍致仕，卒，年六十一，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe he retired as Left Regular Attendant, died at age sixty-one, and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 10 he retired as Left Regular Attendant, died at sixty-one, and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 伯芻風姿古雅，涉學，善談笑，而動與時適，論者稍薄之。

translations.literal: Boqu's bearing was ancient and elegant; he was learned and skilled at witty talk, yet his actions often suited the times, and critics slightly looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Boqu had an ancient, elegant bearing, was learned, and spoke wittily, yet his actions often suited the moment, and critics held him somewhat lightly.

sentences.zh: 子寬夫，登進士第，歷諸府從事。

translations.literal: His son Kuanfu passed the jinshi examination and served as staff officer in various offices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuanfu passed the jinshi examination and served as staff officer in various provincial offices.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，入為監察御史。

translations.literal: During the Baoli era he entered service as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoli era he entered service as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言曰：「近日攝祭多差王府官僚，位望既輕，有乖嚴敬。

translations.literal: He once submitted, saying: 'Recently acting sacrifices have often assigned princely establishment officials; their rank and standing are already light, which violates solemn reverence.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted: 'Recently acting sacrifices have too often assigned officials from princely establishments. Their rank is too low, which violates solemn reverence.

sentences.zh: 伏請今後攝太尉，差尚書省三品已上及保傅賓詹等官；

translations.literal: I submit that hereafter for acting as Grand Marshal one should assign officials of third rank and above in the Department of State Affairs and such officers as mentors, tutors, guests, and stewards;
translations.idiomatic: I beg that hereafter, for acting as Grand Marshal, officials of third rank and above in the Department of State Affairs be assigned, along with mentors, tutors, guests, and stewards;

sentences.zh: 如人少，即令丞郎通攝之。」

translations.literal: if men are few, then let vice directors and directors jointly act in their place.'
translations.idiomatic: if too few are available, let vice directors and directors jointly stand in.'

sentences.zh: 俄轉左補闕。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Left Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 少列陳岵進註《維摩經》，得濠州刺史。

translations.literal: Junior Attendant Chen Hu presented a commentary on the Vimalakirti Sutra and received the prefecture of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Attendant Chen Hu presented a commentary on the Vimalakirti Sutra and was made prefect of Hao.

sentences.zh: 寬夫與同列，因對論之，言岵因供奉僧進經以圖郡牧。

translations.literal: Kuanfu and his colleagues, in audience discussion of the matter, said Hu had presented the sutra through a court-supplied monk in order to seek a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanfu and his colleagues argued in audience that Hu had presented the sutra through a court monk in order to win a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 敬宗怒謂宰相曰：「陳岵不因僧得郡，諫官安得此言，須推排頭首來。」

translations.literal: Jingzong angrily told the chancellors: 'Chen Hu did not receive his prefecture through a monk—how can remonstrance officials say such a thing? The ringleader must be identified and brought forward.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong angrily told the chancellors, 'Chen Hu did not win his prefecture through a monk. How can remonstrance officials say such a thing? Identify the ringleader and bring him forward.

sentences.zh: 寬夫奏曰：「昨論陳岵之時，不記發言前後，唯握筆草狀，即是微臣。

translations.literal: Kuanfu submitted: 'When Chen Hu was discussed yesterday, I do not remember who spoke before or after; I alone held the brush and drafted the memorial—that was I.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanfu submitted, 'When Chen Hu was discussed yesterday, I cannot recall who spoke when. I alone held the brush and drafted the memorial. That was I.

sentences.zh: 今論事不當，臣合當罪。

translations.literal: If the discussion was improper, I ought to bear the guilt.
translations.idiomatic: If the discussion was improper, I alone should bear the guilt.

sentences.zh: 若尋究推排，恐傷事體。」

translations.literal: If investigation and identification are pursued, I fear the matter's integrity will be harmed.'
translations.idiomatic: If you pursue investigation and identification, I fear the affair itself will be harmed.'

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其引過，欣然釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him for taking blame and gladly released the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him for accepting blame and gladly let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 寬夫弟端夫，為太常博士，駁韋綬謚議知名。

translations.literal: Kuanfu's younger brother Duanfu was a Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, famous for opposing Wei Shou's posthumous title proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanfu's younger brother Duanfu was an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, famous for opposing Wei Shou's posthumous title proposal.

sentences.zh: 寬夫子允章、煥章。

translations.literal: Kuanfu's sons were Yunzhang and Huanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanfu's sons were Yunzhang and Huanzhang.

sentences.zh: 允章登進士第，累官至翰林學士承旨、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Yunzhang passed the jinshi examination and rose through offices to Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhang passed the jinshi examination and rose to Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 咸通九年，知貢舉，出為鄂州觀察使、檢校工部尚書，後遷東都留守。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xiantong he oversaw the examinations, was sent out as observation commissioner of Ezhou and acting Minister of Works, and later transferred to be defender of the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong 9 he oversaw the civil examinations, was sent out as commissioner observing Ezhou and acting Minister of Works, and later became defender of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯洛陽，允章不能拒，賊不之害，坐是廢於家。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao attacked Luoyang, Yunzhang could not resist; the bandits did not harm him, but for this he was dismissed and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao attacked Luoyang, Yunzhang could not resist. The rebels did not harm him, but he was dismissed and lived at home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: =袁高=袁高，字公頤，恕己之孫。

translations.literal: Yuan Gao, courtesy name Gongyi, was the grandson of Shuji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gao, courtesy name Gongyi, was the grandson of Shuji.

sentences.zh: 少慷慨，慕名節。

translations.literal: In youth he was generous and aspired to fame and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was generous and aspired to integrity and renown.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，累辟使府，有贊佐裨益之譽。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to commissioner offices, with a reputation for beneficial assistance.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs, with a reputation for effective assistance.

sentences.zh: 代宗登極，征入朝，累官至給事中、御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Daizong ascended the throne, he was summoned to court and rose through offices to Drafting Attendant and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong ascended the throne, Gao was summoned to court and rose to Drafting Attendant and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，擢為京畿觀察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong he was promoted to observation commissioner of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 2 he was promoted to commissioner observing the capital region.

sentences.zh: 以論事失旨，貶韶州長史，復拜為給事中。

translations.literal: For remonstrance that missed the emperor's intent he was demoted to senior administrator of Shaozhou and later reappointed Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His remonstrance displeased the throne and he was demoted to senior administrator of Shaozhou, then reappointed Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，德宗復用吉州長史盧杞為饒州刺史，令高草詔書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, Dezong again employed Lu Qi, senior administrator of Jizhou, as prefect of Raozhou and ordered Gao to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 Dezong again appointed Lu Qi, former senior administrator of Jizhou, prefect of Raozhou and ordered Gao to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 高執詞頭以謁宰相盧翰、劉從一曰：「盧杞作相三年，矯詐陰賊，退斥忠良。

translations.literal: Gao took the draft text and called on chancellors Lu Han and Liu Congyi, saying: 'Lu Qi served as chancellor for three years, deceitful, treacherous, and secretive, driving away the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: Gao took the draft and called on chancellors Lu Han and Liu Congyi, saying, 'Lu Qi served as chancellor for three years, deceitful, treacherous, and secretive, driving away the loyal.

sentences.zh: 朋附者咳唾立至青雲、睚眥者顧盼已擠溝壑。

translations.literal: Those who joined his faction reached the clouds with a cough or spit; those who crossed him with a glance were already pushed into ditches.
translations.idiomatic: His followers rose to the clouds with a cough; those who crossed him were pushed into the ditch with a glance.

sentences.zh: 傲很明德，反易天常，播越鑾輿，瘡痍天下，皆杞之為也。

translations.literal: Arrogant toward bright virtue, he reversed Heaven's constants, drove the imperial carriage into exile, and scarred all under Heaven—all was Qi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant toward virtue, he reversed Heaven's order, drove the emperor into exile, and scarred the realm—all was Qi's doing.

sentences.zh: 爰免族戮，雖示貶黜，尋已稍遷近地，若更授大郡，恐失天下之望。

translations.literal: He was spared clan extermination and though shown demotion, he was soon moved somewhat nearer; if a great commandery is now granted, I fear the hope of all under Heaven will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: He was spared clan extermination and though demoted, was soon moved nearer the capital. If a great prefecture is granted now, I fear you will lose the hope of the realm.

sentences.zh: 惟相公執奏之，事尚可救。」

translations.literal: Only if the chancellors firmly memorialize can the matter still be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Only if you chancellors firmly memorialize can the matter still be saved.

sentences.zh: 翰、從一不悅，改命舍人草之。

translations.literal: Han and Congyi were displeased and changed the order, having an attendant draft it instead.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Congyi were displeased and had an attendant draft the edict instead.

sentences.zh: 詔出，執之不下，仍上奏曰：「盧杞為政，窮極兇惡。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, he held it and would not promulgate it, still submitting: 'Lu Qi's governance reached the utmost in vicious evil.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, he held it and refused to promulgate it, submitting further: 'Lu Qi's governance was utterly vicious and evil.

sentences.zh: 三軍將校，願食其肉；

translations.literal: Officers of the three armies wished to eat his flesh;
translations.idiomatic: Officers of the three armies wished to eat his flesh;

sentences.zh: 百辟卿士，嫉之若讎。」

translations.literal: the hundred ministers hated him as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: the hundred ministers hated him as an enemy.

sentences.zh: 遺補陳京、趙需、裴佶、宇文炫、盧景亮、張薦等上疏論奏。

translations.literal: Supplementation censors Chen Jing, Zhao Xu, Pei Ji, Yuwen Xuan, Lu Jingliang, Zhang Jian, and others submitted memorials arguing the point.
translations.idiomatic: Supplementation censors Chen Jing, Zhao Xu, Pei Ji, Yuwen Xuan, Lu Jingliang, Zhang Jian, and others submitted memorials in support.

sentences.zh: 次日，又上疏。

translations.literal: The next day they submitted again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they submitted again.

sentences.zh: 高又於正殿奏云：「陛下用盧杞獨秉鈞軸，前後三年，棄斥忠良，附下罔上，使陛下越在草莽，皆杞之過。

translations.literal: Gao again submitted in the main hall: 'Your Majesty employed Lu Qi alone to hold the scales of power for three years, casting out the loyal and good, currying favor below and deceiving above, causing Your Majesty to wander in the wilds—all Qi's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Gao again addressed the throne in the main hall: 'Your Majesty employed Lu Qi alone as chancellor for three years, casting out the loyal, currying favor below and deceiving above, and driving Your Majesty into exile—all Qi's fault.

sentences.zh: 且漢時三光失序，雨旱不時，皆宰相請罪，小者免官，大者刑戮。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Han times when the three luminaries lost order and rain and drought came untimely, chancellors all pleaded guilty—minor cases meant removal from office, major cases meant execution.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times, when the heavens fell out of order and rain and drought came untimely, chancellors pleaded guilty—minor faults meant removal, major faults meant execution.

sentences.zh: 杞罪合至死，陛下好生惡殺，赦杞萬死，唯貶新州司馬，旋復遷移。

translations.literal: Qi's crime deserved death; Your Majesty loves life and hates killing and pardoned him from ten thousand deaths, only demoting him to militia commander of Xinzhou, yet soon moved him again.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's crime deserved death. Your Majesty loves life and hates killing and pardoned him from death, demoting him only to militia commander of Xinzhou, yet soon moved him again.

sentences.zh: 今除刺史，是失天下之望。

translations.literal: Now appointing him prefect is to lose the hope of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Appointing him prefect now would lose the hope of the realm.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖意裁擇。」

translations.literal: I prostrate myself in hope that Your sagely intent will decide.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decide.

sentences.zh: 上謂曰：「盧杞有不逮，是朕之過。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Where Lu Qi fell short, it was my fault.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Where Lu Qi fell short, the fault was mine.'

sentences.zh: 復奏曰；

translations.literal: He submitted again:
translations.idiomatic: Gao submitted again:

sentences.zh: 「盧杞奸臣，常懷詭詐，非是不逮。」

translations.literal: 'Lu Qi is a treacherous minister who constantly harbored deceit—it was not a matter of falling short.
translations.idiomatic: 'Lu Qi was a treacherous minister who constantly harbored deceit. It was not a matter of falling short.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕已有赦。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I have already issued an amnesty.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'I have already issued an amnesty.'

sentences.zh: 高曰：「赦乃赦其罪，不宜授刺史。

translations.literal: Gao said: 'An amnesty pardons crime; he should not be made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, 'An amnesty pardons crime. He should not be made prefect.

sentences.zh: 且赦文至優黎民，今饒州大郡，若命奸臣作牧，是一州蒼生，獨受其弊。

translations.literal: Moreover, the amnesty text was most generous to the black-haired people; Raozhou is a great commandery—if a treacherous minister is made its shepherd, the common people of one province alone will suffer the harm.
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty was most generous to the people. Raozhou is a great prefecture. If a traitor is made its governor, the people of that province alone will suffer.

sentences.zh: 望引常參官顧問，並擇謹厚中官，令采聽於眾。

translations.literal: I hope regular-attendance officials may be consulted and careful, solid inner attendants chosen to gather and hear from the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that regular-attendance officials be consulted and careful inner attendants chosen to gather opinion from the people.

sentences.zh: 若億兆之人異臣之言，臣當萬死。」

translations.literal: If the hundred million people differ from your subject's words, your subject deserves ten thousand deaths.'
translations.idiomatic: If the people disagree with me, I deserve ten thousand deaths.'

sentences.zh: 於是，諫官爭論於上前，上良久謂曰：「若與盧杞刺史太優，與上佐可乎？」

translations.literal: Thereupon remonstrance officials argued before the throne; after a long while the emperor said: 'If making Lu Qi prefect is too generous, would making him senior administrator suffice?'
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon remonstrance officials argued before the throne. After a long silence the emperor said, 'If prefect is too generous, would senior administrator suffice?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「可矣！」

translations.literal: They said: 'That will do!'
translations.idiomatic: They said, 'That will do!'

sentences.zh: 遂追饒州制。

translations.literal: The Raozhou appointment edict was then recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The Raozhou appointment was then recalled.

sentences.zh: 翌日，遣使宣慰高云：「朕思卿言深理切，當依卿所奏。」

translations.literal: The next day an envoy was sent to comfort Gao, saying: 'I have reflected on your words—they are profound in principle and urgent in point; I shall follow what you submitted.'
translations.idiomatic: The next day an envoy was sent to comfort Gao, saying, 'I have reflected on your words. They are profound and urgent. I shall follow what you submitted.'

sentences.zh: 太子少保韋倫、太府卿張獻恭等奏：「袁高所奏至當，高是陛下一良臣，望加優異。」

translations.literal: Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Wei Lun, Minister of the Imperial Treasury Zhang Xiangong, and others submitted: 'Yuan Gao's memorial was entirely appropriate; Gao is a good minister of Your Majesty—I hope he may receive special favor.'
translations.idiomatic: Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Wei Lun, Minister of the Imperial Treasury Zhang Xiangong, and others submitted, 'Yuan Gao's memorial was entirely right. Gao is a good minister of Your Majesty. I hope he may receive special favor.'

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，上以關輔祿山之後，百姓貧乏，田疇荒穢，詔諸道進耕牛，待諸道觀察使各選揀牛進貢，委京兆府勸課民戶，勘責有地無牛百姓，量其地著，以牛均給之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, because after the An Lushan rebellion in the Guan region the people were poor and fields lay waste and foul, the emperor ordered all circuits to present plow oxen; each circuit's observation commissioner was to select oxen for tribute, and the Metropolitan Prefecture was charged to encourage farming households, investigate commoners who had land but no oxen, measure their holdings, and distribute oxen evenly.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2, because after the An Lushan rebellion the Guan region's people were poor and fields lay waste, the emperor ordered all circuits to present plow oxen. Each circuit's commissioner was to select oxen for tribute, and the Metropolitan Prefecture was to encourage farming, identify peasants with land but no oxen, measure their holdings, and distribute oxen evenly.

sentences.zh: 其田五十畝已下人，不在給限。

translations.literal: Those with fifty mu of fields or less were not within the distribution limit.
translations.idiomatic: Those with fifty mu of fields or less were excluded from distribution.

sentences.zh: 高上疏論之：「聖慈所憂，切在貧下。

translations.literal: Gao submitted a memorial arguing: 'Your sagely compassion is concerned, and that concern lies urgently with the poor below.
translations.idiomatic: Gao submitted a memorial: 'Your sagely compassion is concerned above all with the poor below.

sentences.zh: 有田不滿五十畝者尤是貧人，請量三兩家共給牛一頭，以濟農事。」

translations.literal: Those with less than fifty mu are especially the poor—I request that two or three households jointly be given one ox to aid farming.
translations.idiomatic: Those with less than fifty mu are especially poor. I beg that two or three households jointly receive one ox to aid farming.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，從之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於官，年六十，中外嘆惜。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office at age sixty; court and countryside sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office at sixty. Court and countryside mourned him.

sentences.zh: 憲宗朝，宰臣李吉甫嘗言高之忠鯁，詔贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Xianzong reign, Chancellor Li Jifu once spoke of Gao's loyal forthrightness, and an edict posthumously made him Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianzong reign Chancellor Li Jifu spoke of Gao's loyal forthrightness, and an edict posthumously made him Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: =段平仲=段平仲，字秉庸，武威人。

translations.literal: Duan Pingzhong, courtesy name Bingyong, was a native of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pingzhong, courtesy name Bingyong, came from Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 隋人部尚書段達六代孫也。

translations.literal: He was the sixth-generation descendant of Duan Da, Minister of the Personnel Office of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was the sixth-generation descendant of Duan Da, Sui Minister of the Personnel Office.

sentences.zh: 登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 杜佑、李復相繼鎮淮南，皆表平仲為掌書記。

translations.literal: Du You and Li Fu in succession governed Huainan and both memorialized to appoint Pingzhong as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Du You and Li Fu governed Huainan in succession and both appointed Pingzhong chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 復移鎮華州、滑州，仍為從事。

translations.literal: When Fu moved to govern Hua and Hua prefectures, Pingzhong still served as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu moved to govern Hua and Hua, Pingzhong continued as his staff officer.

sentences.zh: 入朝為監察御史。

translations.literal: He entered court as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 平仲磊落尚氣節，嗜酒傲言。

translations.literal: Pingzhong was open and bold, esteeming integrity, fond of wine and proud in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong was open and bold, esteemed integrity, loved wine, and spoke with proud directness.

sentences.zh: 時德宗春秋高，多自聽斷。

translations.literal: At the time Dezong was advanced in years and often decided matters himself.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was advanced in years and often decided matters himself.

sentences.zh: 由是庶務壅隔，事或不理，中外畏上嚴察，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Because of this routine affairs were blocked and matters sometimes went unsettled; court and countryside feared the emperor's stern scrutiny and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Routine affairs piled up blocked and matters sometimes went unsettled. Court and countryside feared the emperor's stern scrutiny and none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 平仲嘗謂人曰：「主上聰明神武，臣下畏懼不言，自循默耳。

translations.literal: Pingzhong once told others: 'The sovereign is intelligent and divinely martial; his subjects fear and do not speak—they merely follow in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong once said, 'The sovereign is intelligent and martial. His subjects fear him and stay silent—that is all.

sentences.zh: 如平仲一得召見，必當大有開悟。」

translations.literal: If Pingzhong should once be summoned to audience, he would surely bring great enlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: If I were once summoned to audience, I would surely bring great enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年，京師旱，詔擇御史、郎官各一人，發廩賑恤。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan the capital suffered drought; an edict chose one censor and one director each to open granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 14 the capital suffered drought. An edict chose one censor and one director each to open granaries for relief.

sentences.zh: 平仲與考功員外陳歸當奉使，因辭得對，乃入近禦座，粗陳本事。

translations.literal: Pingzhong and vice director of merit evaluation Chen Gui were to serve on the mission; taking leave he gained audience, approached near the imperial seat, and roughly stated the business.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong and vice director of merit evaluation Chen Gui were chosen for the mission. Taking leave he gained audience, approached the throne, and roughly stated the business.

sentences.zh: 上察平仲意有所蓄，以歸在側不言。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived that Pingzhong had something stored up; because Gui stood beside him and did not speak,
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw that Pingzhong had more to say. Because Gui stood beside him and said nothing,

sentences.zh: 及奏事畢退，平仲獨不退，欲有奏啟；

translations.literal: when the report was finished and they withdrew, Pingzhong alone did not withdraw, wishing to submit further;
translations.idiomatic: when the report ended and they withdrew, Pingzhong alone did not leave, wishing to submit further;

sentences.zh: 上因兼留歸問之，聲色甚厲，雜以他語。

translations.literal: the emperor therefore also detained Gui and questioned him, his voice and expression very stern, mingled with other words.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor detained Gui as well and questioned him in a stern voice, mingling other topics.

sentences.zh: 平仲錯愕，都不得言因誤稱其名。

translations.literal: Pingzhong was startled and could not speak at all, and in error called out his own name.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong was startled speechless and in confusion called out his own name.

sentences.zh: 上怒，叱出之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and shouted him out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and shouted him out.

sentences.zh: 平仲蒼黃，又誤趨禦障後，歸下階連呼，乃得出。

translations.literal: Pingzhong turned pale; again in error he rushed behind the imperial screen; Gui called from the lower steps repeatedly before he could get out.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong turned pale, blundered behind the imperial screen, and only got out when Gui called repeatedly from the lower steps.

sentences.zh: 由是坐廢七年，然亦因此名顯。

translations.literal: For this he sat idle for seven years, yet also thereby became famous.
translations.idiomatic: For this he sat idle seven years, yet thereby became famous.

sentences.zh: 後除屯田膳部二員外郎、東都留守判官，累拜右司郎中。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed vice director of the Farms Office and the Provisions Office, judge under the defender of the eastern capital, and successively promoted to director in the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made vice director of the Farms and Provisions offices and judge under the defender of the eastern capital, and rose to director in the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元和初，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was transferred to Grand Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhe he became Grand Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 內官吐突承璀為招討使，征鎮州，無功而還。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Tu Tu Chenghui served as pacification commissioner, campaigned against Zhen Prefecture, and returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendant Tu Tu Chenghui served as pacification commissioner against Zhen Prefecture and returned without success.

sentences.zh: 平仲與呂元膺抗疏論列，請加黜責。

translations.literal: Pingzhong and Lü Yuanying submitted strong memorials arguing the case and requesting further demotion and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong and Lü Yuanying submitted strong memorials requesting further demotion and punishment.

sentences.zh: 轉給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 自在要近，朝廷有得失，未嘗不論奏，時人推其狷直。

translations.literal: Once in important and close posts, whenever the court had gain or loss he never failed to submit memorials; contemporaries praised his uncompromising uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Once in important posts, whenever the court erred he submitted memorials without fail. Contemporaries praised his uncompromising uprightness.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書左丞，以疾改太子左庶子卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; because of illness he was changed to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died.
translations.idiomatic: He became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; because of illness he was reassigned as Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died.

sentences.zh: =薛存誠=薛存誠，字資明，河東人。

translations.literal: Xue Cuncheng, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Cuncheng, courtesy name Ziming, came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父勝，能文，嘗作《拔河賦》，詞致瀏亮，為時所稱。

translations.literal: His father Sheng was skilled at writing; he once composed the "Tug-of-War Rhapsody," its wording fluent and bright, and was praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng was a skilled writer who once composed the Tug-of-War Rhapsody; its language was fluent and bright, and he was praised by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 存誠進士擢第，累辟使府，入朝為監察御史，知館驛。

translations.literal: Cuncheng passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly summoned to commissioner staffs; he entered court as Investigating Censor and supervised post stations.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng passed the jinshi examination, served repeatedly on commissioner staffs, entered court as Investigating Censor, and supervised the post stations.

sentences.zh: 元和初，王師討劉辟，郵傳多事，上特令中官為館驛使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, when the imperial army campaigned against Liu Pi, postal relay affairs were numerous; the emperor specially ordered inner attendants to serve as post-station commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhe, when the imperial army campaigned against Liu Pi, postal affairs multiplied. The emperor specially ordered inner attendants to serve as post-station commissioners.

sentences.zh: 存誠密表論奏，以為有傷公體。

translations.literal: Cuncheng secretly submitted a memorial arguing that this harmed public propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng secretly submitted a memorial arguing that this injured public propriety.

sentences.zh: 會諫官亦論奏，上乃罷之。

translations.literal: As it happened remonstrating officials also submitted memorials, and the emperor then abolished the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials submitted memorials as well, and the emperor then abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 轉殿中侍御史，遷度支員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Censor and promoted to vice director of the Revenue Office.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Censor and was promoted to vice director of the Revenue Office.

sentences.zh: 裴垍作相，用為起居郎，轉司勛員外、刑部郎中、兼侍御史、知雜事，改兵部郎中、給事中。

translations.literal: When Pei Ji became chancellor, he was used as Diarist; he was transferred to vice director of Merits, director in the Ministry of Justice, concurrently Serving Censor and supervisor of miscellaneous matters, then changed to director in the Ministry of War and Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Ji became chancellor, he was appointed Diarist. He rose to vice director of Merits, director in the Ministry of Justice, concurrent Serving Censor supervising miscellaneous matters, then became director in the Ministry of War and Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 瓊林庫使奏占工徒太廣，存誠以為此皆奸人竄名，以避征役，不可許。

translations.literal: The Qionlin Treasury commissioner reported that registered artisans and laborers were too numerous; Cuncheng considered that these were all scoundrels who slipped in names to avoid corvée and conscription, and should not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Qionlin Treasury commissioner reported that registered artisans and laborers had grown too numerous. Cuncheng argued that scoundrels were slipping in names to avoid corvée and conscription, and the practice should not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 咸陽縣尉袁儋與軍鎮相競，軍人無理，遂肆侵誣，儋反受罰。

translations.literal: Xianyang county magistrate Yuan Dan disputed with a military garrison; the soldiers were without reason, then wantonly slandered and accused him, and Dan in turn was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyang county magistrate Yuan Dan clashed with a military garrison. The soldiers acted without cause, slandered him freely, and Dan was punished instead.

sentences.zh: 二敕繼至，存誠皆執之。

translations.literal: Two edicts arrived in succession, and Cuncheng held to his position on both.
translations.idiomatic: Two edicts arrived in succession, and Cuncheng resisted both.

sentences.zh: 上聞甚悅，命中使嘉慰之，由是擢拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he was greatly pleased, ordered an inner envoy to praise and comfort him, and thereby promoted him to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased when he heard, sent an inner envoy to praise and comfort him, and promoted him to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 僧鑒虛者，自貞元中交結權倖，招懷賂遺，倚中人為城社，吏不敢繩。

translations.literal: The monk Jianxu, from the Zhenyuan era onward, formed ties with the powerful and favored, solicited and accepted bribes, relied on inner attendants as his ramparts, and officials did not dare restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Jianxu had since the Zhenyuan era cultivated ties with the powerful and favored, solicited bribes, relied on inner attendants as his protection, and officials did not dare touch him.

sentences.zh: 會於頔、杜黃裳家私事發，連逮鑒虛下獄。

translations.literal: When private affairs at the homes of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When private scandals at the homes of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 存誠案鞫得奸贓數十萬，獄成，當大辟。

translations.literal: Cuncheng investigated and interrogated, obtaining evidence of corrupt bribes totaling several hundred thousand; when the case was complete, the sentence was death.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng's investigation uncovered corrupt bribes worth several hundred thousand. When the case was complete, the sentence was death.

sentences.zh: 中外權要，更於上前保救，上宣令釋放，存誠不奉詔。

translations.literal: Powerful figures inside and outside court repeatedly interceded before the emperor to save him; the emperor proclaimed an order to release him, but Cuncheng did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful figures inside and outside court repeatedly interceded before the emperor. The emperor ordered Jianxu released, but Cuncheng refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 明日，又令中使詣臺宣旨曰：「朕要此僧面詰之，非赦之也。」

translations.literal: The next day the emperor again sent an inner envoy to the Censorate to proclaim: "I wish to question this monk face to face; this is not a pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor again sent an inner envoy to the Censorate with this order: "I wish to question this monk in person. This is not a pardon.

sentences.zh: 存誠附中使奏曰：「鑒虛罪款已具，陛下若召而赦之，請先殺臣，然後可取。

translations.literal: Cuncheng appended to the inner envoy's report: "Jianxu's crimes are fully established. If Your Majesty summons and pardons him, please kill me first—then you may take him.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng sent a report through the inner envoy: "Jianxu's crimes are fully established. If Your Majesty summons and pardons him, kill me first—then you may take him.

sentences.zh: 不然，臣期不奉詔。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, this subject will surely not obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I will not obey the edict."

sentences.zh: 上嘉其有守，從之，鑒虛竟笞死。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his steadfastness and assented; Jianxu was ultimately beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his steadfastness and agreed. Jianxu was beaten to death in the end.

sentences.zh: 洪州監軍高重昌誣奏信州刺史李位謀大逆，追赴京師。

translations.literal: Hongzhou army supervisor Gao Chongchang falsely memorialized that Xin Prefecture governor Li Wei plotted great treason; Li was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhou army supervisor Gao Chongchang falsely reported that Xin Prefecture governor Li Wei was plotting treason. Li was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上令付仗內鞫問。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him handed over to the inner guard for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him handed over to the inner guard for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 存誠一日三表，請付位於御史臺。

translations.literal: Cuncheng submitted three memorials in one day, requesting that Li Wei be entrusted to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng submitted three memorials in a single day, asking that Li Wei be turned over to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 及推案無狀，位竟得雪。

translations.literal: When the case was investigated and no substance was found, Li Wei was finally cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was investigated and found baseless, Li Wei was finally cleared.

sentences.zh: 未幾，再授給事中。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again appointed Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 數月，中丞闕，上思存誠前效，謂宰相持憲無以易存誠，遂復為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Several months later the vice censor-in-chief post was vacant; the emperor remembered Cuncheng's earlier service and told the chancellor that in upholding the law none could replace Cuncheng, and so restored him as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later the vice censor-in-chief post fell vacant. Remembering Cuncheng's earlier service, the emperor told the chancellor that no one could replace him in upholding the law, and restored him as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 未視事，暴卒。

translations.literal: Before he assumed office he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 憲宗深惜之，贈刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong deeply regretted it and posthumously awarded him Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong deeply mourned the loss and posthumously made him Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 存誠性和易，於人無所不容，及當官禦事，即確乎不拔，士友以是稱重之。

translations.literal: Cuncheng's nature was easygoing and he tolerated all people; yet when holding office and handling affairs he was firmly unyielding—scholars and friends therefore esteemed him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng was easygoing and tolerant of all, yet once in office he was firmly unyielding. Scholars and friends esteemed him for it.

sentences.zh: 子廷老。

translations.literal: His son was Tinglao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Tinglao.

sentences.zh: 廷老謹正有父風，而性通銳。

translations.literal: Tinglao was careful and upright with his father's manner, yet his nature was penetrating and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao was careful and upright in his father's manner, yet his nature was penetrating and sharp.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中為右拾遺。

translations.literal: During the Baoli era he served as Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoli era he served as Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 敬宗荒恣，宮中造清思院新殿，用銅鏡三千片、黃白金薄十萬番。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong was dissolute and unrestrained; within the palace a new hall of the Clear Mind Courtyard was built, using three thousand bronze mirrors and one hundred thousand sheets of gold and silver foil.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong was dissolute and unrestrained. A new hall was built in the palace at the Clear Mind Courtyard, using three thousand bronze mirrors and one hundred thousand sheets of gold and silver foil.

sentences.zh: 廷老與同僚入閣奏事曰：「臣伏見近日除拜，往往不由中書進擬，或是宣出。

translations.literal: Tinglao and his colleagues entered the inner gate to report and said: "Your subject observes that recent appointments often do not proceed through the Secretariat's recommendations, but are sometimes issued by imperial announcement.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao and his colleagues entered the inner gate and said: "We observe that recent appointments often bypass the Secretariat's recommendations and are issued directly by imperial announcement.

sentences.zh: 伏恐綱紀漸壞，奸邪恣行。」

translations.literal: I fear the statutes will gradually decay and wicked men will act at will.
translations.idiomatic: We fear the statutes will erode and the wicked will act at will.

sentences.zh: 敬宗厲聲曰：「更諫何事？」

translations.literal: Jingzong said in a harsh voice: "What else do you remonstrate about?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong said harshly: "What else do you remonstrate about?"

sentences.zh: 舒元褒對曰：「近日宮中修造太多。」

translations.literal: Shu Yuanshang replied: "Recently palace construction is too extensive."
translations.idiomatic: Shu Yuanshang replied: "Recently there has been too much construction in the palace."

sentences.zh: 上色變曰：「何處修造？」

translations.literal: The emperor's expression changed and he said: "Where is construction taking place?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression changed. "Where is construction taking place?"

sentences.zh: 元褒不能對，廷老進曰：「臣等職是諫官，凡有所聞，即合論奏。

translations.literal: Yuanshang could not answer; Tinglao stepped forward and said: "Our office is that of remonstrating officials; whatever we hear, we ought to submit memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshang could not answer. Tinglao stepped forward: "We are remonstrating officials. Whatever we hear, we ought to report it.

sentences.zh: 莫知修造之所，但見運瓦木絕多，即知有用。

translations.literal: We do not know where construction is taking place, but we see transport of tiles and timber in very great quantity and thereby know it is being put to use.
translations.idiomatic: We do not know exactly where the work is, but we see vast amounts of tile and timber being moved, so we know it is under way.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下勿罪臣言。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty not to punish my words."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty not to punish us for speaking."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「所奏已知。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your report is noted."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Your report is noted."

sentences.zh: 尋加史館修撰。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally appointed Historiographer of the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally appointed historiographer of the History Office.

sentences.zh: 時李逢吉秉權，惡廷老言太切直。

translations.literal: At the time Li Fengji held power and hated Tinglao's words as too blunt and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji held power at the time and resented Tinglao's blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 鄭權因鄭註得廣州節度，權至鎮，盡以公家珍寶赴京師以酬恩地。

translations.literal: Zheng Quan, through Zheng Zhu, obtained the Guangzhou military commission; when Quan reached his command, he sent all the state's precious treasures to the capital to repay the source of his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Quan obtained the Guangzhou commission through Zheng Zhu. When Quan reached his post, he sent all the state's precious treasures to the capital to repay his patron.

sentences.zh: 廷老上疏請按權罪，中人由是切齒。

translations.literal: Tinglao submitted a memorial requesting investigation of Quan's crimes; inner attendants thereby gnashed their teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao submitted a memorial demanding an investigation of Quan's crimes. Inner attendants gnashed their teeth at him.

sentences.zh: 又論逢吉黨人張權輿、程昔範不宜居諫列，逢吉大怒。

translations.literal: He also argued that Li Fengji's faction members Zhang Quanyu and Cheng Xifan were unfit to hold remonstrating posts; Fengji was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Li Fengji's allies Zhang Quanyu and Cheng Xifan were unfit for remonstrating posts. Fengji was furious.

sentences.zh: 廷老告滿十旬，逢吉乃出廷老為臨晉縣令。

translations.literal: When Tinglao's leave reached ten ten-day periods, Fengji sent Tinglao out as magistrate of Linjin County.
translations.idiomatic: When Tinglao's leave reached one hundred days, Fengji exiled him to serve as magistrate of Linjin County.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，入為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he entered court as Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he entered court as Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，以本官充翰林學士，與同職李讓夷相善。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe, with his existing rank he served as Hanlin Academician and was on good terms with his colleague Li Rangyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 4 he was appointed Hanlin Academician while retaining his existing rank and was on good terms with his colleague Li Rangyi.

sentences.zh: 廷老之入內署，讓夷薦挈之。

translations.literal: Tinglao's entry into the inner secretariat was through Rangyi's recommendation and sponsorship.
translations.idiomatic: Rangyi recommended and sponsored Tinglao's entry into the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 廷老性放逸嗜酒，不持檢操，終日酣醉，文宗知之不悅。

translations.literal: Tinglao's nature was unrestrained and fond of wine; he did not maintain self-restraint, was drunk all day, and Wenzong knew of it and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao was unrestrained and fond of wine. He kept no discipline and was drunk all day. Wenzong knew and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 五年，罷職，守本官，讓夷亦坐廷老罷職，守職方員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was removed from office but kept his nominal rank; Rangyi also because of Tinglao was removed from office and kept only vice director of the Service Office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was removed from the Hanlin post but kept his nominal rank. Rangyi was removed as well because of Tinglao and kept only his post as vice director of the Service Office.

sentences.zh: 廷老尋拜刑部員外郎，轉郎中，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Tinglao was soon appointed vice director in the Ministry of Justice, transferred to director, and promoted to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao soon became vice director in the Ministry of Justice, then director, and was promoted to Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 開成三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kaicheng 3.

sentences.zh: 廷老當官舉職，不求虛譽，侃侃於公卿之間，甚有正人風望。

translations.literal: Tinglao in holding office performed his duties, sought no empty reputation, spoke plainly among dukes and ministers, and had greatly the bearing of an upright man.
translations.idiomatic: In office Tinglao performed his duties without seeking empty fame. He spoke plainly among ministers and bore the reputation of an upright man.

sentences.zh: 贈刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 子保遜，登進士第，位亦至給事中。

translations.literal: His son Baoxun passed the jinshi examination and also rose to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoxun passed the jinshi examination and also rose to Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 保遜子昭緯，乾寧中為禮部侍郎，貢舉得人，文章秀麗。

translations.literal: Baoxun's son Zhaowei, during the Qianning era served as Vice Minister of Rites; his examinations selected worthy men and his essays were elegant and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxun's son Zhaowei served as Vice Minister of Rites in the Qianning era. His examinations selected worthy men, and his writing was elegant.

sentences.zh: 為崔胤所惡，出為磎州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was hated by Cui Yin, was sent out as governor of Xi Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin hated him and had him sent out as governor of Xi Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: =盧坦=盧坦，字保衡，河南洛陽人，其先自范陽徙焉。

translations.literal: Lu Tan, courtesy name Baoheng, was a native of Luoyang in Henan; his ancestors had moved there from Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tan, courtesy name Baoheng, came from Luoyang in Henan. His ancestors had moved there from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 父巒，贈鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Luan was posthumously awarded Governor of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luan was posthumously made Governor of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坦嘗為義成軍判官，節度使李復疾篤，監軍使薛盈珍慮變，遽封府庫，入其麾下五百人於使牙，軍中恟々；

translations.literal: Tan once served as judge of the Yicheng Army; when military commissioner Li Fu was gravely ill, army supervisor Xue Yingzhen fearing trouble suddenly sealed the treasury, brought five hundred men under his command into the commissioner's headquarters, and the army was in uproar;
translations.idiomatic: Tan once served as judge of the Yicheng Army. When military commissioner Li Fu fell gravely ill, army supervisor Xue Yingzhen, fearing trouble, suddenly sealed the treasury and brought five hundred of his own men into headquarters. The army was in uproar;

sentences.zh: 坦密言於盈珍促收之。

translations.literal: Tan secretly told Yingzhen to hasten to withdraw them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan secretly urged Yingzhen to withdraw them at once.

sentences.zh: 及復卒，坦護喪歸東都。

translations.literal: When Fu died, Tan escorted the coffin back to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu died, Tan escorted the coffin back to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 後為壽安令。

translations.literal: Later he served as magistrate of Shou'an.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as magistrate of Shou'an.

sentences.zh: 時河南尹征賦限窮，而縣人訴以機織未就；

translations.literal: At the time the Henan intendant's tax collection deadline was exhausted, yet the county people pleaded that weaving on looms was not yet finished;
translations.idiomatic: The Henan intendant's tax deadline had passed, but the county people pleaded that their loom weaving was not yet finished;

sentences.zh: 坦請延十日，府不許。

translations.literal: Tan requested a ten-day extension; the prefecture office did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan requested a ten-day extension. The prefecture refused.

sentences.zh: 坦令戶人但織而輸，勿顧限也，違之不過罰令俸耳。

translations.literal: Tan ordered households simply to weave and deliver payment, not minding the deadline; if they violated it he would merely forfeit the magistrate's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Tan told the households to keep weaving and pay when ready, ignoring the deadline. If punished, he would forfeit only his own salary as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 既成而輸，坦亦坐罰，由是知名。

translations.literal: When the weaving was finished and payment delivered, Tan also received punishment, and thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: When the weaving was done and payment delivered, Tan accepted punishment himself and thereby became known.

sentences.zh: 累遷至庫部員外郎、兼侍御史、知雜事。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to vice director of the Storehouse Office, concurrently Serving Censor and supervisor of miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the Storehouse Office, concurrent Serving Censor supervising miscellaneous matters.

sentences.zh: 會李锜反，有司請毀锜祖父廟墓。

translations.literal: When Li Qi rebelled, the responsible offices requested destruction of Qi's grandfather's temple and tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qi rebelled, the responsible offices requested destruction of Qi's grandfather's temple and tomb.

sentences.zh: 坦常為锜從事，乃上言曰：「淮安王神通有功於草昧。

translations.literal: Tan had once served Li Qi as aide, and therefore submitted a statement saying: "Prince Huai'an Li Shentong had merit in the founding struggle.
translations.idiomatic: Tan had once served under Li Qi and submitted a statement: "Prince Huai'an Li Shentong earned merit in the founding struggle.

sentences.zh: 且古之父子兄弟，罪不相及，況以锜故累五代祖乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, in antiquity father and son, elder and younger brother—punishment did not extend to one another; how much less should the fifth-generation ancestor be implicated because of Qi?
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity fathers and sons, brothers and brothers did not suffer for one another's crimes. How much less should a fifth-generation ancestor be punished because of Qi?

sentences.zh: 乃不毀。

translations.literal: The request was therefore not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 因賜神通墓五戶，以備灑掃。

translations.literal: Thereupon five households were granted to Shentong's tomb for sweeping and maintenance.
translations.idiomatic: Five households were granted to maintain Shentong's tomb.

sentences.zh: 及武元衡為宰相，以坦為中丞，李元素為大夫，命坦分司東都，未幾歸臺。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanheng became chancellor, Tan was made vice censor-in-chief and Li Yuansu chief censor; Tan was ordered to serve separately at the eastern capital, and before long returned to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanheng became chancellor, Tan was made vice censor-in-chief under chief censor Li Yuansu. Tan was posted separately to the eastern capital and soon returned to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 裴均為僕射，在班逾位，坦請退之，均不受。

translations.literal: Pei Jun was Grand Mentor and in court rank exceeded his proper place; Tan requested that he withdraw, but Jun did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun was Grand Mentor and stood out of rank in court assembly. Tan asked him to withdraw, but Jun refused.

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「姚南仲為僕射，例如此。」

translations.literal: Tan said: "When Yao Nanzhong was Grand Mentor, the precedent was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "When Yao Nanzhong was Grand Mentor, the precedent was the same.

sentences.zh: 均曰：「南仲何人？」

translations.literal: Jun said: "Who was Nanzhong?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun said: "Who was Nanzhong?"

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「南仲是守正而不交權幸者也。」
